blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The reviewed EVM GLDT source is an Ownable ERC-20 whose owner controls minting and burn/withdraw bridge operations; the route review identifies the owner/minter as a single off-chain bridge signer. No separate direct holder blacklist or freeze function is documented, but the issuer-operated bridge and physical-gold custody route remain inherited control and failure-domain exposure.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: GLDT is native to the Internet Computer (GLDT ledger canister 6c7su-kiaaa-aaaar-qaira-cai); its Ethereum/Base/Arbitrum deployments share address 0x86856814e74456893cfc8946bedcbb472b5fa856 via deterministic deployment, not an omnichain standard. The verified EVM source is a custom OpenZeppelin ERC20+Ownable+ERC20Permit token with an owner-only payable mint() (proven on-chain: non-owner calls revert with OwnableUnauthorizedAccount) plus withdrawEth and burn1-burn4 functions that emit bytes32 data encoding the ICP destination, with no LayerZero/Wormhole/Axelar/Hyperlane/CCIP imports (no OFT or CCIP selectors in the deployed bytecode). The contract was deployed by 0x475c65F3f34b069d3e8382090e6e17859b194a5e, which then transferred ownership; the live owner/minter on all three EVM chains is the active EOA 0x70ae25592209b57f62b3a3e832ab356228a2192c, a Gold-DAO-controlled off-chain bridge signer. This makes GLDT's EVM supply a centralized issuer-operated lock/mint bridge with a single third-party off-chain control surface and no published settlement/attestation controls.
